fields.v: (a) Single-shot specification control: complete paper/specification given in one prompt upfront; (b) emergent specification: design disclosed progressively over ~60 coding requests; (c) ProjectGuard (authors' own): external project-state layer for specification tracking. No versions

ProjectGuard: semantic state as filesystem graph of markdown records (design, decision, resource) plus an edge table (EDGES.csv); structural state (repository skeleton: files, class/function signatures, interface relations, refreshed from git); per-turn project-aware task brief; rendered project brief for restarts. Benchmark (not prescribed to the agent): canonical specification, atomic component checklist, latent trajectory (10-20 versions), request scripts

ProjectGuard, per coding turn: forecaster combines current request, request history and semantic + structural state into a brief -> coding agent executes -> semantic helper extracts committed additions/revisions and a merger updates the graph; structural helper refreshes skeleton from git diff -> proactive restart with injected project brief when remaining context is insufficient. Conditions (a)/(b) have no prescribed phases
Not stated (scripted, agent-blind requests; no human in the loop during runs)
Full workflow of ProjectGuard on both platforms; single-shot vs emergent are specification-delivery conditions only

Not stated / not classifiable in Böckeler terms. Single-shot = full spec upfront; ProjectGuard keeps a revisable, continuously updated project state ('committed but revisable project knowledge') alongside the code (closest to spec-anchored, draft)

rev.why: Authors use no SDD terms. ProjectGuard keeps a revisable design record next to the code (spec-anchored reading), but it is an agent memory layer rather than a specification the developer maintains, so 'not classifiable' is equally defensible.

fields.v: New project: implement an ML paper's method from scratch in a fresh repository
20 papers; 10-49 verifiable components per paper (mean 18.6, total 371); 48-61 coding requests per script (mean 57.4, total 1148); 10-20 latent versions per paper
ML research code: methods from 10 ICML 2025 and 10 NeurIPS 2025 papers (optimisation, equivariant networks, diffusion models, RL, interpretability, LLM text detection, autonomous driving, etc.)
N/A (no human participants; two annotators only for judge calibration)
None for agent runs (no tokens, time or money). ProjectGuard overhead only: external memory size (KB) and change in compaction events per session

MCF (mean component faithfulness, 0-4 rubric: absent/wrong/simplified/equivalent/faithful); IF50 = (MCF/4 + DIR)/2, primary endpoint; counts of fully faithful (score 4) and severe failures (score <=1); SLUMP = IF50/MCF/DIR gap single-shot minus emergent; test pass rate of agent-authored tests (shown to have low correlation with IF50, i.e. it fails to detect SLUMP)

rev.why: Draft said test pass rate was 'correlated with IF50'; the paper says the correlation is low and that test pass rate fails to detect SLUMP (Fig. 3, p. 6).

fields.v: DIR (dependency integration ratio: share of public symbols exported by standalone modules reused by downstream integration code), used as structural integration
None

Benchmark exposure audit: recoverable component rate RCR 0.994, explicitly specified rate ESR 0.666, 358/371 components committed and recoverable; judge-human agreement (weighted kappa, exact match, Spearman)

Automatic: bounded LLM judge (max 8 repository-inspection tool calls per component; judge model not stated) scores final repository against frozen components; calibrated on 120 stratified component-run pairs against 2 blinded human annotators (weighted kappa 0.882-0.927 judge-human, 0.930 inter-annotator). Benchmark assets generated by claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 with frozen prompts, 5 papers audited manually. DIR computed from code (procedure not detailed). Wilcoxon signed-rank tests

Criterion: component-faithfulness rubric vs frozen checklist; IF50 primary. Agent models and versions not stated for any configuration. (1) Single-shot + Claude Code + model n.s.: MCF 3.031, DIR 0.303, IF50 0.530. Quality partly; cost not measured. (2) Emergent + Claude Code + n.s.: MCF 2.718, DIR 0.149, IF50 0.414; 118/371 fully faithful, 72 severe failures. Quality partly (does not work on integration); cost not measured. (3) Single-shot + Codex + n.s.: MCF 3.245, DIR 0.289, IF50 0.550. Quality partly; cost not measured. (4) Emergent + Codex + n.s.: MCF 3.242, DIR 0.148, IF50 0.479. Quality partly; cost not measured. (5) Emergent + ProjectGuard + Claude Code + n.s.: MCF 3.000; 181/371 fully faithful; 49 severe failures; IF50 improved on 15/20 (median recovery +34%); DIR median +12%; memory 390 KB mean; compaction median -1. Quality works (relative to emergent); cost not measured (overhead small). (6) Emergent + ProjectGuard + Codex + n.s.: MCF +0.05 (W/L 9/9); DIR improved on 15/19 (mean +76%, median +55%); memory 286 KB; compaction +23 mean (restarts). Quality partly; cost not measured

Tasks: 20 ML papers (Table 5). Configurations: 2 platforms (Claude Code, Codex) x 2 conditions (emergent, single-shot) = 80 runs (20 x 2 x 2); plus emergent + ProjectGuard on both platforms. Baseline: single-shot control for SLUMP; plain emergent for ProjectGuard. Held constant: platform, model family and tooling within each platform; same frozen scripts and components. Acceptance tests: none; LLM-judge rubric on frozen component checklist. Repetitions: Not stated (apparently 1 run per paper x condition). Human intervention: none (scripted requests)

rev.why: Draft marked '80 runs [sic]', but 20 papers x 2 conditions x 2 platforms = 80 is consistent; no error in the paper.

fields.v: Single-shot > emergent on IF50: Claude Code 16/20 papers, mean gap +0.116, Wilcoxon p=0.0003; Codex 14/20, +0.071, p=0.012 (significant). MCF gap Claude Code 0.313, Codex 0.003 (negligible); DIR roughly halves on both. ProjectGuard vs emergent: Claude Code MCF 2.718 -> 3.000 (90% of MCF gap recovered; 13/4/3 W/T/L), fully faithful +53%, severe failures -32%, IF50 better on 15/20; Codex MCF negligible, DIR +76% mean on 15/19. No significance test for ProjectGuard

Distinguished conditions on both platforms (significant IF50 gaps); agent-written test pass rate did not detect SLUMP (low correlation with IF50). Judge reliability checked against humans. Repeatability: single run per condition, not assessed. Limitations stated: synthetic interaction scripts; endpoint-only measure, no causal mechanism; residual LLM-annotation error; single-shot is a matched control, not an upper bound; only 2 platforms and 20 ML papers

20 ML papers, 2 commercial platforms, mathematically structured method implementation; may differ for broader SE tasks. Synthetic scripts may differ from real user behaviour. No within-session temporal degradation measured; MCF/DIR not a complete causal account. LLM-based construction and scoring may carry error. ProjectGuard is a case study: no ablation of its components, generalisation to more platforms and comparison with other memory/context-management baselines not established. Gap: specification tracking as a distinct evaluation target

Agent models/versions and judge model not stated; only construction model snapshot given (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929). Inconsistency: single-shot described as receiving 'the complete specification' (p. 2) vs 'the complete paper in one prompt' (p. 5); Table 6 caption 'full-paper minus emergent'. Abstract '90% of the faithfulness gap' refers to the MCF gap, not IF50 (IF50 recovery median +34%). Table 6 (p. 16) jumbled in pdftotext; values used from text p. 7 and 18 and Table 3 (p. 6). Benchmark 'open-sourced on Github', no URL in text; ProjectGuard code availability not stated. Full construction and judge prompts in App. A.2. Pre-registration: not claimed. Programming language: not stated (Python inferred from .py file names in the example)
